_note: Local congregations (and, for Crete, a network of city congregations) named in the New Testament, together with the people Scripture explicitly ties to each by name. This is not claimed as an exhaustive catalog of every incidental mention -- per CLAUDE.md's Factual Accuracy rules, only affiliations the text itself states are included, and unnamed figures (e.g. the Philippian jailer, Philip's four prophesying daughters) are not given invented names. A person appearing under more than one church reflects Scripture recording them at more than one congregation over time. `role` is left null where the text names someone without stating a function or title.

churches.name: Jerusalem
churches.description: The first church, born when the Holy Spirit fell on the disciples at Pentecost. It grew rapidly under the apostles' teaching and the believers' shared life, weathered its own early scandal when Ananias and Sapphira lied to the church about a gift, and became the site of the council (Acts 15) that settled how Gentile believers should be received.

churches.name: Antioch (Syria)
churches.description: The first church with a large Gentile membership, and the place believers were first called "Christians." It commissioned Paul and Barnabas for what became the first missionary journey, and was later the flashpoint for the debate over circumcising Gentile converts that the Jerusalem council settled -- including a sharp public rebuke Paul gave Peter here over table fellowship with Gentiles.

churches.name: Antioch (Pisidia)
churches.description: A synagogue congregation on Paul and Barnabas's first missionary journey where Paul's sermon drew wide interest, provoked jealousy from some of the synagogue leaders, and led the two to turn deliberately toward preaching to the Gentiles.

members.role: preached in the synagogue; expelled from the region by opponents
preached alongside Paul; expelled from the region by opponents

churches.name: Iconium
churches.description: A city where Paul and Barnabas saw a large number of Jews and Greeks believe, but fled after a plot to stone them was uncovered -- one of the persecutions Paul later reminded Timothy he had endured.

members.role: preached with Barnabas; fled a stoning plot
preached with Paul; fled a stoning plot

churches.name: Lystra
churches.description: The city where a crowd first tried to worship Paul and Barnabas as gods, then stoned Paul and left him for dead, and where -- on Paul's return visit -- a young disciple named Timothy joined him as a missionary companion.

churches.name: Derbe
churches.description: A city Paul and Barnabas reached after Paul's stoning at Lystra, where they made many disciples before retracing their steps to strengthen the churches they had planted.

members.role: preached with Barnabas, making many disciples
preached with Paul

churches.name: Philippi
churches.description: The first church Paul planted in Europe, begun with a small group of women praying by a river. Paul and Silas were later beaten and jailed here, and the church that grew from this beginning became one of Paul's most affectionate and financially generous partners in the gospel.

churches.name: Thessalonica
churches.description: A church founded during a brief but fruitful three-week synagogue ministry, whose faith Paul says "rang out" well beyond Macedonia -- even though its founding provoked a mob and a formal complaint to the city officials.

churches.name: Berea
churches.description: Praised by Luke for examining the Scriptures daily to test Paul's teaching -- "more noble-minded" than Thessalonica -- resulting in many believing before agitators arrived from Thessalonica to stir up trouble.

churches.name: Athens
churches.description: Not a settled congregation so much as the beginning of one -- Paul's reasoning in the synagogue, the marketplace, and finally before the Areopagus council produced a mixed response, but a small number believed, including a member of that council.

members.role: reasoned in the synagogue and marketplace, then addressed the Areopagus

churches.name: Corinth
churches.description: A church Paul planted during an eighteen-month stay, drawn from a cosmopolitan, morally loose port city, and one whose factions, lawsuits, and tolerance of gross sin gave Paul more to correct by letter than almost any other congregation -- while also including believers of real social standing, like its city treasurer.

churches.name: Cenchreae
churches.description: Corinth's eastern port church, known from a single verse commending its servant Phoebe as she carried Paul's letter to the Romans.

members.role: servant (deacon) of the church; carried Paul's letter to Rome

churches.name: Ephesus
churches.description: Paul's longest single ministry base -- about three years -- growing into a major church later addressed by name in Ephesians, Timothy's two pastoral letters, and the first of the seven letters in Revelation, which commends its perseverance and doctrinal discernment but warns it has "left its first love."

churches.name: Colossae
churches.description: A church Paul never personally visited, planted instead through his co-worker Epaphras, and best known today as the recipient of the letter defending Christ's supremacy against an early mix of philosophy and legalism -- and as the home church of the runaway slave Onesimus and his master Philemon.

churches.name: Laodicea
churches.description: A wealthy neighboring church to Colossae, told to exchange letters with them, and later addressed by name in the last and sharpest of Revelation's seven letters -- rebuked as "lukewarm" and warned that its material wealth had masked spiritual poverty.

members.role: hosted a house church here

churches.name: Rome
churches.description: A church Paul had not founded and had not yet visited when he wrote Romans, already large enough for him to send greetings to over two dozen named believers scattered across several house congregations; he later reached the city himself as a prisoner, and still had fellow believers with him during his second imprisonment there.

churches.name: Crete
churches.description: Not a single congregation but a network of city churches across the island, left in an unfinished state -- Paul left Titus behind specifically to "set in order what remains" and appoint qualified elders in every town.

members.role: left here by Paul to complete the work and appoint elders in every city

churches.name: Smyrna
churches.description: A persecuted and materially poor church -- "you are rich" -- that receives the second of Revelation's seven letters, with no rebuke, only a warning of coming suffering and a promise of the crown of life.

churches.name: Pergamum
churches.description: A church commended for holding fast "even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells," though also rebuked for tolerating false teaching within its ranks.

members.role: "My faithful witness," killed here for his faith

churches.name: Thyatira
churches.description: Commended for growing love, faith, service, and perseverance, but rebuked for tolerating a self-proclaimed prophetess -- called "Jezebel" after the Old Testament queen -- who was leading believers into sexual immorality and idolatry.

churches.name: Sardis
churches.description: Told bluntly that it has "a name that you are alive, but you are dead" -- the only one of the seven churches given no commendation at all, though a few there "have not soiled their garments."

churches.name: Philadelphia
churches.description: Along with Smyrna, one of only two of the seven churches to receive no rebuke -- praised for keeping Christ's word despite "little power," and promised an open door no one can shut.

churches.name: Troas
churches.description: A coastal city where believers gathered to break bread on the first day of the week -- the setting for Paul's all-night sermon during which a young man dozed off, fell from a third-story window, and was raised back to life.

members.role: preached through the night here on his final journey to Jerusalem
fell asleep during Paul's long sermon, fell from a window, and was raised up alive

churches.name: Samaria
churches.description: The first church outside Judea proper, planted when persecution scattered believers from Jerusalem -- Philip's preaching and miracles drew large crowds, including a well-known sorcerer whose profession of faith Peter later called into serious doubt.

members.role: evangelist; preached Christ and performed signs that drew large crowds
sorcerer who professed belief and was baptized, then rebuked by Peter for trying to buy the Spirit's power with money

churches.name: Caesarea
churches.description: Home to the first recorded Gentile convert and his household -- a turning point Peter later cited at the Jerusalem council -- and later the settled base of the evangelist Philip and his household.

members.role: Roman centurion; first Gentile convert, with his household, in the account that opened the door to Gentile inclusion
settled here after his evangelistic travels; hosted Paul and his companions

churches.name: Joppa
churches.description: Home to Tabitha (Dorcas), a disciple whose death and raising by Peter led many in the city to believe, and to Simon the tanner, whose house Peter was staying in when he received the vision that opened the gospel to Gentiles.

members.role: disciple known for good works and charity; raised from death by Peter
tanner who hosted Peter
